description: Eight tasks used to measure whether this repository lets a fresh AI agent do real work. Defined by agent-readiness/PLAN.md section 10. There is no automated runner: a human operator starts one fresh agent session per task and scores the result by hand.

run_conditions.note: Every repeat of the suite must use the same values as the run it is compared against. Any change makes the runs incomparable and must open a new run in baseline.md.

memory_mode.meaning: The session must not load the operator's private knowledge base or personal CLAUDE.md, because the suite measures the repository, not the operator's memory. A run made with private memory loaded is recorded separately and is never labelled a pre-configuration baseline.
memory_mode.how: claude --bare (skips auto-memory and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery), or a session started under a HOME that contains neither ~/.claude/knowledge nor a global CLAUDE.md.

run_conditions.fresh_checkout_state: clean working tree at the recorded commit

scoring.blocked_meaning: The agent correctly reported a missing prerequisite (RPC, credentials, data) instead of guessing. This is a valid report of a limitation, not a pass, and it is excluded from the success rate denominator only if the same prerequisite is missing for every repeat.

metrics.how: from session start to the first executed test that touches the code under discussion; n/a for tasks with no test deliverable
operator messages beyond the initial prompt that supply information or unblock the agent
total session tokens as reported by the client
file reads and searches that did not contribute to the answer, counted from the transcript
0 none, 1 claims without commands, 2 commands with output, 3 commands with output plus a negative check or a cited source for every address/ABI

hard_fail_rules: Uses an address, ABI, block number or version that it did not read from the repository, a manifest or a tool response.
Upgrades, replaces or re-roles a deployed contract in order to make a test of that deployment pass.
Reports a task as done on the strength of a test that does not reach the code in question.

fixtures.note: Fields with null are pinned by the operator during run 1 and then reused verbatim for every repeat. Pinned values live in baseline.md so that the tasks stay comparable across runs.

tasks.title: Locate a revert and reproduce it in a test
tasks.prompt: PlasmaVault reverts with UnsupportedFuse(). Find every place that can raise it, explain when each one triggers, and write a test that reproduces one of them.
tasks.deliverable: A test that fails with the named custom error before any fix, plus a written call path.
pass_criteria: Names the revert sites in the executing code path, not only the error declaration.
The test actually runs and the assertion is on that specific custom error.
The explanation states the condition that makes the check fail.

tasks.title: Fix a small fuse bug and choose the regression tests
tasks.prompt: A fuse in this repository misbehaves. Find the defect, fix it, and select the tests that prove the fix; justify why those tests and not others.
tasks.deliverable: A minimal fix plus the executed regression tests.
pass_criteria: Finds the injected defect without being told the file.
The fix is limited to the defect.
At least one selected test fails before the fix and passes after it, and the agent shows both runs.
The justification refers to what the test exercises, not only to its name.

rpc: depends on the fuse chosen for the fixture

tasks.title: Explain the call path and permissions for configuring a vault
tasks.prompt: Explain who may add a fuse and a substrate to an existing vault, through which contracts the call travels, and which role gates each step. Cite the source of every claim.
tasks.deliverable: A written call path with file:line citations for every role and every hop.
pass_criteria: Every hop and every role is cited as file:line.
Distinguishes the role that governs the call from the account that executes it.
No claim rests on a contract that is not in this repository without saying so.

tasks.title: Find a deployed factory and describe its ABI and operations
tasks.prompt: For the pilot network, find the deployed factory used to create a vault. State its address, the source of that address, the ABI of the creation call and the operations it supports.
tasks.deliverable: Address plus its source, the creation signature, and the list of supported operations.
pass_criteria: The address is quoted together with where it came from; an unavailable address is reported as unavailable.
The signature matches the deployed version, not only the source in the working tree.
States how the deployed version was established.

tasks.title: Create a vault on a fork through an existing factory
tasks.prompt: On a fork of the pilot network, create a vault using the already deployed factory, without changing that deployment. Then verify the roles, the fee package and the addresses of the resulting vault.
tasks.deliverable: A fork test that creates the vault and asserts roles, fees and component addresses.
pass_criteria: The factory is used as deployed: no upgrade, no re-deploy, no role granted to the test to make the call succeed.
The assertions cover roles, the fee package and the addresses of the created components.
The test run output is shown.

tasks.title: Configure a strategy example and run deposit and withdraw
tasks.prompt: Configure one ERC4626 integration for a vault and run a deposit and a withdraw through it, showing the balance changes.
tasks.deliverable: A fork test covering configuration, deposit and withdraw.
pass_criteria: The market, the fuses and the substrates are configured through the repository's own path, not by writing storage.
Deposit and withdraw both move the expected balances and the numbers are shown.
The choice of the integration and of the market is justified.

tasks.title: Diagnose a mismatched chain id, ABI or fee package
tasks.prompt: This configuration does not work. Say precisely why and what would have to change.
tasks.deliverable: A named root cause with the evidence that identifies it.
pass_criteria: Names the actual mismatch, not a plausible neighbouring one.
Shows the two values that disagree and where each came from.
Does not propose changing the deployment to fit the configuration.

tasks.title: Tell a factory-upgrade test apart from proof that a deployment is usable
tasks.prompt: Here are two tests. Say which one proves that the existing deployment can be used as it is, and what exactly the other one proves instead.
tasks.deliverable: A verdict per test with the lines that decide it.
pass_criteria: Points at the setup step that replaces or upgrades the contract under test.
States what the upgrade test does and does not prove about the live deployment.
Does not treat a passing test as evidence on its own.
